ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Republic of Korea: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 16580, as amended), particularly Article 5-2 on customer identification and beneficial owner verification; Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment; Act on Prohibition of Financing and Spread of Weapons of Mass Destruction; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; Financial Services Commission regulations implementing customer due diligence and UBO identification; Commercial Act for shareholder registers and corporate governance. Where the ultimate group includes a China WFOE, PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 (effective Nov 1, 2024) mandates that UBO information is Government_Only_Access.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Company Registration Certificate / Certificate of Registered Facts)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registry of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the destination state is an Apostille Convention member: obtain the certified court-issued certificate, then affix the Apostille certificate from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. If the destination state is not an Apostille member: obtain the certified court-issued certificate, obtain confirmation of the court seal and signature at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then submit to the destination state Embassy/Consulate in Seoul for consular legalization. The apostille path and consular legalization path are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Court Registry Confirmation of No Liquidation, Dissolution, Bankruptcy or Cancellation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registry of the District Court of the registered office, supplemented by the National Tax Service business registration record
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille states: request a certified English/Korean good-standing extract from the court, then apostillize through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. For non-Apostille states: have the court extract certified, authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and then legalized by the consular post of the destination country in Seoul. The two legalization routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; an apostille must not be combined with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Chusik Hoesa, authenticated by a licensed Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille states: notarize the board resolution and signatures, then obtain the Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. For non-Apostille states: notarize the board resolution, obtain Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, and complete consular legalization at the destination state consulate in Seoul. The authorization documents must state the precise scope, counterparty and banking/payment rail purposes, and the two authentication paths must never be applied sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court Internet Registration Office / official registry extract and notarized original Articles of Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille states: certify the registered Articles, then attach Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For non-Apostille states: certify the registered Articles, obtain Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, and then perform consular legalization at the destination country embassy/consulate in Seoul. The apostille and consular legalization tracks are separate alternatives, never cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean licensed bank branch (e.g., Shinhan, Kookmin, Hana, Woori or equivalent) holding the corporate account or validating the corporate relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille states: have the bank officer sign the reference letter before a notary, notarize the signature, and obtain an Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For non-Apostille states: notarize the bank officer signature, authenticate through the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and legalize at the destination state consulate in Seoul. The bank letter must explicitly cover transaction history, AML standing, account conduct, and beneficial owner relation, and the apostille/consular routes must not be combined.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to incorporation and throughout the AEO supply-chain audit relationship, counsel shall screen every subscriber, beneficial owner, director, officer, authorized signatory, bank account controller, commercial counterparty, freight forwarder, payment recipient and beneficiary using a licensed global real-time screen against OFAC SDN/Consolidated Sanctions List, UN Security Council consolidated and country-specific lists, EU consolidated list, UK OFSI consolidated list, Interpol notices where legally permissible, and the Korean Government consolidated financial sanctions list under the Act on Prohibition of Financing and Spread of Weapons of Mass Destruction; each person shall undergo Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) screening using a reputable vendor database with risk-flagging and enhanced due diligence for PEPs, family members and close associates; automated screening shall run continuously at a minimum daily frequency with case management escalation, and negative news and ownership linkage searches shall be preserved in the AML/CFT file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (Commercial Registry electronic name search) and National Tax Service Business Registration Name Search portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official corporate name and type designation must be registered in Korean (Hangul); the type identifier 'Chusik Hoesa' or the Hangul equivalent must appear in the registered name; foreign words are permitted only in phonetic Hangul transliteration unless a specific statutory exception applies; the name must satisfy a four-tier convention comprising corporate type designation, distinctive trade name, business purpose and registered office; any English trade name used in contracts must be recorded in the Articles of Incorporation but does not replace the Hangul legal name for registry, tax or customs purposes.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry portal or commercial registrar rejects a proposed name on grounds of confusing similarity, non-compliance with Hangul transliteration rules, or use of a prohibited or sensitive token, the applicant shall file a written objection to the responsible registrar within 14 days from the rejection notice, attaching a legal opinion distinguishing the proposed name from pre-existing marks under Commercial Act Article 23 and demonstrating that any sensitive token has been approved by the competent regulator. If the registrar maintains the rejection, the applicant may appeal to the competent administrative court within 90 days, or file a provisional disposition petition to prevent registration of a competing name; a professionally drafted name-clearance memorandum citing registry search results and regulated-token approval evidence is essential before re-filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a Chusik Hoesa engaged in AEO certification and security auditing, a virtual office, commercial mailbox, shared desk or registered-agent-only address will not satisfy the commercial substance standard expected by the National Tax Service, the Korea Customs Service or Korean financial institutions. The National Tax Service mandates a physical business address for business registration and tax invoices; banks and the Wise open-banking/KYB flow reject virtual addresses because the entity requires a verifiable operating presence, records preservation, and security controls; Korea Customs Service AEO validation includes on-premises security and audit controls, so a physical principal office and data room in the registered jurisdiction are mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced inspection risk is HIGH (80-95%) for Korea Customs Service AEO certification and audit because customs officers conduct physical validation and post-certification security verifications; MODERATE (40-60%) for National Tax Service visits after business registration, especially within the first two years; LOW-MODERATE (20-30%) for municipal local tax office presence verification; LOW (10%) for registry or court postal and address verification. The checklist includes physical office lease agreement in Korean, business registration plate, tax invoices, employment records, VAT returns, UBO and board minute files, visitor logs, CCTV and security procedures, server and log retention, and evidence of real supply-chain audit capacity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act (Sangbeop, Act No. 1000, as amended), particularly Articles 288 to 317 (incorporation of stock corporations), Article 383 (board of directors), Article 393 (powers of the board), Article 408 (representative director), and Article 409 et seq. (statutory auditor); supplemented by the Commercial Registration Rules and, where foreign equity is present, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registry Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office; filings may be lodged online through the Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea (https://irs.srt.re.kr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation (Ju-sik Ho-sa Seol-lip Deung-gi Sin-cheong-seo), accompanied by the notarized articles of incorporation, capital deposit certificate, organizational meeting minutes, and board appointment consents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Chusik Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act. The articles of incorporation must state the number and par value of shares, and all issued shares must be fully subscribed. Before registration, the total subscription money must be deposited into a blocked incorporation deposit account maintained at a domestic financial institution; such funds may not be withdrawn until the Commercial Registry completes the incorporation registration. After issuance of the certificate of incorporation, the blocked capital is released to the company's operating account. Non-resident investment is permitted and is separately reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, but no minimum block amount is imposed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (A CHUSIK HOESA), NUMBER ONE, DULY ADOPTED, AT [PLACE], ON THIS [__] DAY OF [__], 20__.

The First Board of Directors of the company, having been elected at the statutory organizational meeting held on [date], and being present in their full complement, hereby record and adopt the following resolutions.

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ISSUANCE. RESOLVED, that the board has examined the subscription schedules and confirmatory bank certificates presented by the incorporators and hereby accepts, approves, and ratifies the subscription and payment for [number] ordinary shares, of par value KRW [value], issued for a total stated paid-in capital of KRW [amount]. This board confirms that the entire subscription money has been deposited in a blocked incorporation deposit account maintained at [bank name and branch] pursuant to Article 306 of the Korean Commercial Act. The board authorizes the Representative Director, immediately following the issuance of the certificate of incorporation registration, to instruct the bank to release such funds from the blocked incorporation account and to transfer them into the company's operating current account. Such transfer shall be recorded in the company's books as fully paid capital, and the Corporate Secretary shall file amendments, if any, with the district registry.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the board hereby opens, maintains, and operates current, savings, foreign-currency, and settlement accounts at [bank name], and that the corporate seal and the manual signatures of the Representative Director and any two directors jointly, as set out in the bank's signature schedule, shall bind the company. The board delegates to the Representative Director authority to negotiate payment collection, discharge of liabilities, and foreign exchange settlements for the company's customs-AEO supply-chain audit engagements, subject to the internal expenditure limits appended to these minutes.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the company shall be located at [full street address, ward, city, Republic of Korea], which shall be legally treated as the principal place of business for service of process, tax registration, and commercial registration. The board directs the Representative Director to record the registered office in the Commercial Registry and to update the same whenever the office is relocated.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED, that the board appoints [Name] as Representative Director, [Name] as Director, [Name] as Auditor, and [Name] as Corporate Secretary, each to hold office until the next Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders. The Representative Director is vested with general management power, representation before all public authorities, and execution of the company's incorporation, tax, customs, labor, and environmental filings. Any statutory auditor shall perform the functions required by Articles 409 through 412 of the Korean Commercial Act. The officers accept their appointments and agree to act in compliance with Korean law and the articles of incorporation.

5. GENERAL BUSINESS POWERS. RESOLVED, that any one of the officers is authorized to execute all commercial instruments, management-consultancy contracts, AEO security-audit agreements, and compliance reports required by clients, and to engage counsel, certified public accountants, customs consultants, and other professionals as necessary.

6. EFFECTIVENESS. RESOLVED, that these resolutions shall take effect immediately and remain in force until amended by a subsequent board resolution or shareholder resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Search and Drafting of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office of the District Court having jurisdiction over the intended registered office; electronic look-up through the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (https://irs.srt.re.kr).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before drafting the definitive articles, the promoters must confirm that the proposed Korean company name is not identical or deceptively similar to an existing legal name shown on the Commercial Register. The Korean Commercial Act does not permit a later company name exactly equal to an already registered domestic corporate name. After the name is found available, the promoters execute and sign the articles of incorporation, including the corporate objects of management consultancy and AEO supply-chain security auditing, total shares, par value, directors, and fiscal year. The incorporators must ensure that the business-object statement captures ISIC 7020 services and incidental customs-audit advisory activities. The articles must then be sent to a notary public for attestation before proceeding to capital deposit.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of identification of every incorporator and director
Written application confirming the proposed company name
Power of attorney if signed by an agent
Draft articles of incorporation (Jeong-gwan) in Korean
Statement of share subscription (Ju-sik In-chaek-seo)
Evidence of identity and address for each subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the name as confusingly similar, the promoters should file an alternative name selection by lodging a supplementary filing with the Commercial Registry; no hearing is required. If the notary refuses attestation because the articles omit mandatory items under Article 289 of the Korean Commercial Act, correct the text and resubmit the articles without requiring a new formal organizational meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles and Opening of Blocked Capital Deposit Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Certified Korean notary public registered under the Ministry of Justice, and a domestic commercial bank supervised by the Financial Supervisory Service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators must appear before a notary public to certify the articles of incorporation, proving that all subscribers agreed on the contents and that the notary's seal is affixed. Simultaneously, a blocked incorporation deposit account at a domestic bank must be opened in the name of the proposed company or the promoters. Each subscriber must remit the total subscription price into that account, and the bank will issue a certificate of deposit of subscription money stating the amount and the restriction on withdrawal until registration. This certificate must be addressed to the district registry and submitted with the incorporation application. At least one director shall execute the account documents and confirm that no funds will be withdrawn before the Commercial Registry completes registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized articles of incorporation (original and prescribed copies)
Share subscription form for each subscriber
Certificate of deposit of paid-in capital from the Korean bank
Incorporators' identity evidence and power of attorney if any
Copy of the bank account application and blocked-deposit instruction
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines to issue a deposit certificate until the proposed name registration is complete, the promoters may use a representative depository arrangement by paying into the trust account of an attorney-at-law and attaching the attorney's certificate of deposit. If the notary requires clarification of the object clause, amend the articles and republish the approval, ensuring the revised text is attached to the final application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Registration to the Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Division (Deung-gi-gwa) of the District Court of the registered office; online via the Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoters, or a professional agent holding a power of attorney, must file the incorporation registration with the court having jurisdiction over the registered office. The registration application must include the certificate of deposit of subscription money, the notarized articles of incorporation, minutes of the organizational meeting, resolutions and consents of officers, identification documents, and the specimen of the corporate registered seal. The registry will examine whether the corporate object is lawful, whether paid-in capital is fully subscribed, and whether the officers are qualified. Upon clearance, the court issues the certificate of incorporation registration, legal personality is constituted, and the company becomes a valid Chusik Hoesa.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation (Ju-sik Ho-sa Seol-lip Deung-gi Sin-cheong-seo)
Original notarized articles of incorporation
Original certificate of deposit of subscription money
Minutes of the organizational meeting and first board meeting
Consent and appointment letters of directors, auditor, and corporate secretary
Power of attorney if filing through an agent
Specimen of corporate seal and corporate seal registration certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry demands correction or issues a summary suspension, counsel must file supplementary corrections through the same registry portal within the prescribed period, usually no later than two weeks. If the deficiencies are not cured, the application may be rejected; re-filing with the full corrected dossier is generally faster than appealing under the Non-Contentious Case Procedure Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration, Tax Registration, and Corporate Seal Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office (Se-mu-seo) of the National Tax Service through the HomeTax portal, together with the municipal office for local tax registration and the Foreign Investment Ombudsman/KOTRA if foreign investment reporting applies.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after incorporation registration, the Representative Director must file a business registration application with the tax office of the company's place of business, in accordance with the Value-Added Tax Act and the Corporate Tax Act. The application must state the company registration number, registered office address, business classification code 70200 (management consultancy) and associated customs-audit advisory services, and bank account information. The National Tax Service will issue a business registration certificate together with value-added tax and corporate tax identifiers. The company must also register its corporate seal impression with the court and issue share certificates to shareholders. If a non-resident investor made a reportable foreign investment, the report must be filed with the designated acquiring bank or KOTRA under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration
Notarized articles of incorporation
Lease contract or address certification for the registered office
Representative director identification and specimen seal
Corporate seal registration certificate
Foreign investment report receipt or exemption letter, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If business registration is queried because of inadequate address evidence, submit a lease agreement or ownership certificate. If the tax office requires correction of the business classification code, revise the application immediately through HomeTax. No penalty is assessed if the correction is made within the statutory filing period and before taxable transactions have commenced.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation, Capital Release, and Industrial Licensing Assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank branch that issued the blocked-deposit certificate, with reference to the Korea Customs Service and municipal authorities only if a future physical logistics operation is established; for pure ISIC 7020 consulting activity, no industrial licensing authority applies.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the certificate of incorporation registration is delivered, the directors must attend the opening bank with the corporate seal, the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, corporate seal registration certificate, and director identification to convert the blocked incorporation deposit into an unrestricted operating account. The bank verifies the completed registration and releases the paid-in capital. Concurrently, the compliance officer should conduct a licensed-activity assessment for the intended business. ISIC 7020 management consultancy and AEO-certification security auditing is a non-licensed professional service under Korean law. No manufacturing, chemical, assembly, warehouse, environmental, or civil-defense fire license is required if the company operates exclusively as an office-based consultancy. If the company later opens physical facilities, a new Stage 2 assessment will be required before operations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration
Original bank certificate of blocked deposit
Corporate seal registration certificate
Director identification and bank signature card
Completed account-operating and anti-money-laundering questionnaire
Copy of business registration certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires further documentation, provide a board resolution approving the account opening and capital release. If funds are not released within the bank's normal processing window, escalate to the bank's compliance officer under the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions. Because no industrial license applies, no adverse environmental or civil-defense cure is required for the current consulting-only scope.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industrial or physical operation is carried out under ISIC 7020 (management consultancy and AEO supply-chain compliance audit services). If the company were to add physical warehousing, assembly, or manufacturing in the future, the competent authorities would be the Ministry of Environment, the relevant municipal government, and the National Fire Agency, and a supplementary Stage 2 analysis would be required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - for the current office-based consultancy activity, no environmental permit is required. The statutory environmental authority in Korea is the Ministry of Environment (Hwan-gyeong-bu), but it has no jurisdiction over this digital/consulting operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the company generates no wastewater discharge unit, no VOC-emitting process, and no hazardous waste generator status. If a physical logistics facility is later established, the Clean Air Conservation Act, Water Environment Conservation Act, and Waste Management Act thresholds would be evaluated at that time.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - the company has no physical premises requiring civil defense fire inspection or structural load certification. As a consultancy with an office, fire-safety compliance is limited to the building's existing consolidated fire safety certificate issued under the Act on Fire Prevention and Safety of Buildings, and the employer's general duties under the Occupational Safety and Health Act to maintain a safe workplace. If the company later operates a warehouse or assembly site, it must obtain the appropriate National Fire Agency permit and workplace approval from the Ministry of Employment and Labor before commencing those operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax System (hometax.go.kr). Export declarations are separately processed through the Korea Customs Service (KCS) UNI-PASS electronic customs clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine whether the entity is a domestic corporation (Chusik Hoesa incorporated under the Korean Commercial Act) or a foreign non-resident entity. Step 2: For a Korean domestic corporation, the representative must file an Application for Business Registration with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the principal place of business prior to commencing business. The application can be submitted through the HomeTax portal (hometax.go.kr) or in person at the competent district tax office. Attach the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, resolution appointing directors, proof of place of business (lease contract or ownership certificate), and, where there are non-resident shareholders, a tax residence certificate and Korean-language translations of relevant corporate documents. Step 3: For a foreign non-resident entity, the NTS assigns a Business Registration Number (Korean TIN/VAT ID) upon submission of the statutory business registration application and designation of a local tax representative or tax agent under Article 82 of the Framework Act on National Taxes. The tax representative accepts service of process and carries out filing obligations. Step 4: The 10-digit Business Registration Number issued by the NTS serves as both the Corporate Tax Identification Number and the Value Added Tax (VAT) registration number; it must be used on tax invoices, electronic tax invoices, customs declarations, and all tax filings. Step 5: Foreign non-resident suppliers of electronically supplied services to Korean customers may register through the simplified VAT registration procedure for overseas suppliers, appoint a Korean tax agent, and use the HomeTax portal even without a Korean place of business. Step 6: Maintain the registration continuously; any change in company name, address, business type, or legal representative must be reported through HomeTax within 15 days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Chusik Hoesa is a domestic corporation and is taxed at entity level on its worldwide income under the Corporate Tax Act. Non-resident shareholders are not directly taxable on corporate profits except through dividend withholding tax upon distribution; the entity does not qualify for pass-through treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not maintain a check-the-box or elective entity classification regime under national tax law. A Chusik Hoesa is per se an entity-level taxpayer. Anti-hybrid mismatch rules derived from the OECD BEPS Project apply mandatorily to prevent double deduction or deduction without inclusion outcomes; no elective hybrid election is available to taxpayers.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Korean Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover-based exemption threshold applies to corporations; every person engaged in business is required to register for VAT with the National Tax Service before commencing business. A simplified taxation regime with an annual taxable supply threshold of KRW 80,000,000 applies only to qualifying individual sole proprietors, not to Chusik Hoesa corporations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered entrepreneurs, and corporations in particular, are required to issue an Electronic Tax Invoice (e-tax invoice) through the HomeTax system or an approved ASP. The e-tax invoice must be transmitted automatically to the NTS in near real time on the date of issuance, and no later than the day after issuance. Each e-tax invoice is assigned a unique digital control number generated and validated by the NTS, and the system operates as an anti-fraud clearance mechanism without requiring a physical fiscal stamp. The e-tax invoice must include the 10-digit Business Registration Numbers of both supplier and recipient, the supply date, item description, supply value, VAT amount, and serial number. VAT returns are filed semi-annually through HomeTax, and export refund claims are also adjudicated electronically.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value Added Tax Act, goods that are exported from Korea are zero-rated, and services supplied in or used for the performance of export business or services performed and consumed outside Korea may also be zero-rated. For AEO certification, supply-chain compliance auditing, digital content, game distribution, and cross-border consulting services, the taxpayer must prove that the recipient is a non-resident with no Korean place of business, that the place of supply and actual consumption are outside Korea, that the service is not connected with Korean real estate or goods located in Korea, and that the consideration is paid in foreign currency or in Korean won through a documented foreign-exchange transaction. Merely invoicing a non-resident is insufficient; the service must be actually rendered and supported by contemporaneous documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration issued through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS electronic clearance system; the export declaration number is the primary statutory evidence of physical export and zero-rating eligibility)
Transport document: Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) demonstrating physical cross-border movement of goods from Korea to the foreign buyer

Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or Foreign Exchange Sales Certificate issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing actual receipt of export proceeds from the non-resident counterparty

Commercial Invoice, Packing List, purchase order or service contract, and a detailed service-delivery or audit report evidencing the foreign recipient, the nature of the AEO audit services supplied, and the overseas place of supply and consumption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service, in coordination with the Korea Customs Service, subjects zero-rated export refund claims to documentary scrutiny and may require online verification of the export declaration, vessel or aircraft movement, and bank ledger showing foreign exchange repatriation. If export proceeds are not collected or repatriated within 180 days from the export declaration date, or if the zero-rating is otherwise unsupported by the customs and foreign-exchange documentation bundle, the NTS will deny the zero rating, reassess VAT at 10% on the supply value, and impose statutory additional tax for understating the VAT base. Additional dues include the daily additional tax on overdue national taxes (0.022% per day from the statutory filing deadline until payment) and the underreporting penalty under the Framework Act on National Taxes. A false or fraudulent export tax invoice can trigger the illegal tax invoice penalty, criminal referral for tax evasion, imprisonment not exceeding five years, and a fine not exceeding KRW 100 million. For an AEO-certified entity, the Korea Customs Service may additionally suspend or revoke AEO authorization, remove expedited clearance privileges, and re-audit historical export transactions, exposing earlier VAT refunds to retrospective clawback with interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea, together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Foreign Exchange Information System which enforce the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act of South Korea
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a predominantly liberalized current account convertibility regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, while capital account transactions are broadly open but require declaration, filing, or approval through an authorized foreign exchange bank for circumstances such as foreign direct investment, overseas borrowings, issuance of securities, and cross-border loans. Export proceeds and current account receipts are freely convertible and may be held in foreign currency accounts without mandatory surrender to the central bank, reflecting the transition from the former surrender requirement regime to a settlement and reporting system. Dividend remittances and profit repatriation by foreign shareholders are permitted after corporate tax clearance, audited financial statements, and submission of an income source verification to the bank; no broad exchange control approval is required, but the remitting bank must file a foreign exchange purpose code and maintain supporting documentation for suspicious transaction monitoring. Capital account repatriation of the original invested amount also carries reporting obligations through the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and the Foreign Exchange Information System. In practice, non-residents face documentation friction rather than convertibility denial, and banks must verify the underlying real demand principle before executing large FX conversions. Overall, KRW is freely usable for trade and ordinary business purposes, with residual compliance rails for capital movements, anti-money laundering screening, and evidentiary preservation of the underlying corporate purpose.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Trade Regulations, export receipts must be collected within the statutory payment period, generally within 18 months from the date of export declaration unless an extension is approved by the Ministry of Economy and Finance, and must be received through an authorized foreign exchange bank or reported to the Foreign Exchange Information System. There is no mandatory conversion ratio into KRW; the exporter may hold export proceeds in a foreign currency account under the foreign exchange bank's custody. However, the exporter is obligated to report the collection and holding of export proceeds, retain supporting trade documents such as the bill of lading, commercial invoice, customs export declaration, and a certificate of collection from the bank, and respond to any banking sector due diligence requests. Failure to collect within the prescribed period must be explained, and funds used outside the permitted trade settlement cycle may be treated as a contravention of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and subject to administrative penalties.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. Foreign fintech EMIs and digital-only banking platforms are not licensed as banks by the Financial Supervisory Service and cannot independently provide full corporate accounts or Korean won settlement rails to a Korean-domiciled Chusik Hoesa. EMIs such as Wise may offer payment corridors through local bank partners or via SWIFT, but they are not a substitute for a regulated domestic corporate bank relationship required for capital escrow, foreign investment reporting, trade document handling, VAT refunds, and FEIS filings. A multinational treasury structure can use Wise as a secondary payment execution rail for low-value, non-regulated disbursements, but the primary treasury account must reside with a Tier-1 domestic commercial bank that can accept foreign capital injections and issue the certificate of foreign investment. Any EMI arrangement must be reviewed carefully to ensure it does not trigger unlicensed banking activity, unreliable settlement, or sanctions screening gaps in the Korean jurisdiction.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident shareholder or foreign-appointed director of a Chusik Hoesa, most Korean Tier-1 banks will require the statutory director or an authorized officer with a properly notarized power of attorney to attend a physical in-branch appointment at least once for account activation and signing authority verification. Some banks accept consular proxy opening for corporate accounts if the power of attorney is apostilled or consular-legalized, the beneficial owner's identity is verified through a recognized international KYC database, and a live video interview is conducted with the compliance officer. However, remote-only onboarding without any physical presence is rare for a newly established foreign-owned Korean corporation because the Equal Treatment of Financial Transactions Act and Bank of Korea reporting standards require clear identification of the real controller, source of funds, and the purpose of every foreign exchange transaction. In practice, the safest assumption is that at least one statutory director or the foreign signatory must appear in-branch with a certified corporate seal, entity formation documents, and passport; otherwise a remote notarized appointment must be negotiated before account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership or indirect foreign shareholding structure that makes the controlling shareholder difficult to identify
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO ownership chart up to natural persons, apostilled or consular-legalized certificates of incorporation for each entity in the chain, certified register of shareholders, passport copies of all UBOs, board resolution approving the Korean entity formation and bank account opening, corporate seal registration certificate, and a written source of funds and source of wealth statement for each shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient documentary trail for the initial capital injection or for the source of funds used to build share capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of bank statements from the remitting foreign entity and each indirect shareholder, audited financial statements or certified balance sheet of the investor, tax clearance certificates, evidence of the underlying commercial transaction for capital subscription, sworn source of wealth declaration, and a breakdown explaining inherited assets, business profits, or proceeds from asset disposals; if third-party loans are used, provide a certified loan agreement, interest schedule, and lender KYC documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign corporate documents, powers of attorney, and director signatures that are not authenticated in a format accepted by Korean bank compliance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostille certification from the jurisdiction of incorporation for all entity documents, English-Korean notarized translations, original or certified copies of the articles of incorporation, certificate of good standing, certificate of incumbency, board resolution authorizing the Korean bank account, and a Korean notarized corporate seal certificate showing the exact seal imprint to be used for banking instruments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to trade-based money laundering or sanctions risk because the AEO supply chain audit business may involve high-risk counterparties or dual-use logistics data
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer risk assessment matrix, sanctions screening policy and PEP screening records, proposed client and transaction flow diagrams, AEO certification number and audit credentials, export control classification for the services rendered, control procedures for classified data, professional indemnity insurance policy, and a rolling audit report evidencing the absence of undisclosed related-party trade with sanctioned jurisdictions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital injections into the Korean Chusik Hoesa must be structured under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The foreign investor first files a foreign investment notification with the Foreign Exchange Information System through an authorized domestic bank or Invest Korea; upon acceptance, the investor receives a foreign investment notification certificate. The remittance is then made in the investor's home currency or KRW via SWIFT into a dedicated capital escrow account held in the Korean entity's name at the Tier-1 bank. The bank will map the remittance to the government-purpose code for direct investment capital, usually under the capital account category for FDI subscription, and issue a foreign investment registration certificate and paid-in capital certificate after verification. The Korean entity must then register the paid-in capital with the Korean tax authority, obtain an evidence of foreign inward remittance, and produce a statutory certificate of capital verification before the funds can be moved into the general operating account. Inbound transfers must include accurate beneficiary identifiers, the corporate registration number, the purpose of remittance, the share subscription agreement, and a traceable reference to the foreign investment notification certificate; any mismatch between the remitter and the notified foreign investor will delay compliance clearance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for the AEO audit and supply chain compliance business should be executed through the primary Tier-1 Korean bank using SWIFT MT103 for straightforward fee-based payments, professional service fees, and operating expenses, with standardized payment purpose codes under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. For supply chain trade settlements that require title evidence or documentary security, the treasury should use commercial letters of credit under UCP600, documentary collections under URC522, or bank payment obligations where counterparty credit risk is material. Every outbound trade payment must be supported by service agreements, purchase orders, commercial invoices, customs declarations if goods are involved, internal audit evidence, and where applicable, exchange rate contracts or trade finance facility utilization notices. The Korean bank is required to check that the FX purpose code matches the underlying commercial reality, that the beneficiary is not subject to OFAC/EU/UN sanctions, and that the disbursement amount is consistent with the receivable ledger and transfer pricing policy. Foreign currency invoices from vendors may be settled from the company's foreign currency account or by converting KRW into the invoice currency at the bank's cover rate; high-value disbursements should be approved through a dual-signature matrix to prevent unauthorized clearing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward exchange contracts between the Korean entity and its authorized foreign exchange bank for documented current account and trade settlements
Non-deliverable forward contracts (NDFs) where underlying KRW exposure is supported by genuine trade or direct investment exposure and the counterparty is authorized under Korean FX regulations
Cross-currency swaps for hedging foreign-currency-denominated borrowings related to the Korean entity's working capital or investment obligations
Plain-vanilla currency options for hedging known future import or service fee payments
Exchange-traded or over-the-counter forward structures with a documented real demand principle and no speculative leverage beyond the underlying business exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Tax Return and accompanying financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the year immediately following a December 31 fiscal year-end, or within 3 months after fiscal year-end if a different year-end is adopted; extensions permitted by NTS upon application before due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty: 20% of unpaid tax; under-reporting penalty: 10% of understated tax; late-payment surcharge: NTS statutory daily interest (currently approximately 0.022% per day, compounding to about 9.7% per annum). Continued delinquency exposes business registration to forced cancellation by NTS, leading to loss of power to trade and potential Court-ordered dissolution for a non-operating company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax annual return and payment (attached to corporate tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial or metropolitan local government tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers, by April 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local Tax Act penalties: 20% of unpaid tax for non-filing, 10% for under-reporting, and daily late-payment interest (approx. 0.03% per day) on unpaid amounts. Persistent delinquency can trigger compulsory tax collection and a tax lien on corporate assets, though it does not by itself dissolve the corporation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Enterprise annual report of business performance (only if the Chusik Hoesa is beneficially owned by non-residents per the Foreign Investment Promotion Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: KOTRA or the foreign exchange bank with which the foreign investment was reported
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end; for a December fiscal year, by March 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to KRW 5 million (approx. USD 3,700) per false or non-filed report; the foreign investor may also lose the protections and currency-conversion privileges attached to the certified foreign-invested enterprise status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AEO annual compliance and maintenance report (only if the company holds Korean Customs Service AEO certification)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days after the close of the AEO certification cycle; where the cycle aligns with the fiscal year, no later than March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the annual AEO maintenance report may result in suspension, conditional approval, or revocation of AEO certification under Korea Customs Service enforcement rules, including immediate downgrade to regular customs clearance status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified CPA audit is mandatory under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree if (i) the Chusik Hoesa is a listed company; (ii) the company's total assets exceed KRW 12 billion (approx. USD 8.5 million–9 million) at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year; (iii) the company is a parent or major subsidiary consolidated into an audited group with consolidated assets above the threshold; or (iv) the company is designated as a public-interest company by the Securities and Futures Commission. Small unlisted companies below the asset threshold are exempt unless they voluntarily adopt audit requirements or are otherwise designated.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean IFRS (K-IFRS) is mandatory for listed entities and may be voluntarily adopted by unlisted companies. Unlisted companies below K-IFRS scope report under Korean GAAP (General Corporate Accounting Standards), which aligns with the IFRS for SMEs; smaller companies may use the SME Accounting Standards. All audited financial statements must be prepared on the accrual basis and express a true and fair view in accordance with the External Audit Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a general annual UBO confirmation filing system for domestic private Chusik Hoesa. Periodic shareholding confirmation is achieved indirectly: (a) in the annual Foreign Investment Enterprise Report if the entity has non-resident investors; (b) for any change of shareholding, the shareholders' register (Register of Members) must be updated; (c) if a transfer results in non-resident ownership, the 30-day reporting window to the foreign exchange bank or KOTRA under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act starts on the acquisition date. For resident-to-resident transfers, no annual filing arises; the company's own registers reflect ownership. Statutory registers must be maintained continuously and be available for inspection at the registered office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (Shareholders and Board of Directors)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - 1,800 per year for a typical Korea-registered office or corporate secretarial agent in Seoul
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - 35,000 per year for a small-to-mid-size Chusik Hoesa preparation, audit, and filing package (fees vary with subsidiary count and transaction volume)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% headline top marginal Korean corporate income tax rate on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion; the progressive schedule is 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, and 21%
